analyst_view.overall: Early view: Two mid-to-low-table sides that both like the ball. Javi Calleja's Eldense lost their last two league games without scoring before a round-13 trip to Las Palmas whose result is not yet in these numbers; Ferran Costa's Sabadell are 12th, had a Monday game at home to Real Sociedad II, and will be without Óscar Sanz through a yellow-card ban.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and I agree with a low figure. Eldense have not scored in their last two league games and Sabadell average about a goal a game for and against. Sabadell missing Sanz (two goals) takes a little away, but not enough to go lower than the site already is.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. I lean higher: Sabadell had 66 per cent of the ball and 25 shots at Albacete, the kind of pressure that piles up corners, and Calleja wants Eldense to keep the ball too (they had 59 per cent at home to Granada). Two sides pushing for territory should mean set pieces at both ends.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean lower: two possession-minded sides usually make for fewer tactical fouls, and Eldense's record (28 yellows and no reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures) is one of the cleaner ones. Sabadell's 3.1 away looks a touch high.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. I lean higher: Sabadell took 25 shots at Albacete and Eldense 13 at home to Granada, and with both teams keen on the ball neither should sit in a low block for 90 minutes. Volume is likely; accuracy is the problem for both.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target and I leave it. Both teams create more than they convert: Sabadell's 25 shots at Albacete brought one goal, and Eldense's 13 against Granada none. More attempts than usual, but not many more on target.
